job.Title: Senior Technical Project Manager
job.Description:
Applied Research Associates, Inc. is looking for a Senior Technical Project Manager to join our team! This is an exciting opportunity to help support a growing list of programs involving modernization of explosives and energetic materials production facilities, munitions production, and novel production system design. In this role you will collaborate with project/program managers, explosives and munitions subject matter experts, and federal stakeholders to support research and development capabilities and ongoing production operations. Candidates must be eager to learn, embrace a safety-first mindset, and work effectively with diverse teams, including peers, clients, and stakeholders.

Work Environment Details: This position operates entirely onsite in a high-activity environment that features an open-plan layout collaborative workspace where visual line-of-sight monitoring and immediate verbal team communication are required at all times. The workspace features active operational equipment, standard facility fluorescent light and ambient machinery noise. Regular, in-person interaction with on-site team members in this workspace are essential functions of this role.

Employment is contingent upon the successful attainment of at least an Interim xxxx clearance, granted by the sponsoring agency.

Due to the nature of this work, candidates for this position must be US citizens residing within the US. This position is located at the Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head and will require you to be onsite. This position does not allow for a remote or hybrid work schedule.

Responsibilities Include:

  • Oversee the proper execution of projects, including detailed planning, scheduling, and procurement aligned with customer specifications. Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams and program management counterparts to develop comprehensive plans for technical deliverables and schedules.
  • Develop and implement strategies to meet project objectives while managing scope, schedule, and budget.
  • Monitor project performance and apply change management principles to address scope issues, risks, and resource constraints in collaboration with Project Controls Analysts.
  • Prepare detailed reports for senior leadership on project progress, challenges, and solutions.
  • Engage with subcontractors, federal agencies, corporate partners, and local officials to drive project success.
  • Provide leadership for the safe and cost-effective execution of manufacturing capabilities in complex production environments, in collaboration with federal defense clients.
  • Develop, plan, and execute goals that align with client objectives and ensure timely, quality deliverables. Lead regular client facing meetings to update progress and facilitate technical discussion.
  • Implement and monitor safety and quality programs, ensuring all project staff adhere to contractual terms, scope of work, regulatory requirement, and client specific quality and safety standards.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree engineering, or other related discipline with 8 - 10 years of experience, or a Master's degree with 6 - 8 years of experience.
  • At least 2 years in a supervisory capacity.
  • Proven experience managing DoW or DoE projects involving facilities improvements which include capital expenditure and manufacturing process implementation.
  • Expertise in resource and risk management, with the ability to maximize ROI for large-scale projects.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex projects, including the integration and coordination of diverse stakeholders such as government agencies, contractors, and vendors.
  • Ability to work effectively in high-pressure, dynamic environments, managing rapid changes in project scope, funding, and priorities.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to tailor presentations and reports to diverse technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office suite.
  • US Citizenship and the ability to obtain or maintain a security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Degree in engineering or related technical field.
  • Experience working with federal agencies, including DoW and DOE.
  • Experience in managing production modernization projects/programs, particularly in the design and implementation of new manufacturing capabilities.
  • Active Department of War (DoW) security clearance.
  • PMP certification or equivalent project management training.

Applied Research Associates, Inc. is a 100% employee-owned international research and engineering company recognized for providing technically superior solutions to complex and challenging problems in the physical sciences. We invite you to visit our website to learn more about who we are, what we do, the excellent careers and each of the competitive benefits we offer and explore some of our featured offices.

 

Anticipated Salary Range: $135,000 - $150,000

job.Title: Mechanical Engineer
job.Description:
Who We Are

Neya Systems is a recognized leader in off-road autonomy and mission orchestration software, delivering cutting-edge robotic solutions for defense, commercial, and industrial applications. As a wholly owned subsidiary of Applied Research Associates (ARA), we develop ruggedized, field-proven platforms designed to solve complex, unstructured environments' toughest challenges.

Who We’re Looking For

We are a dedicated group of innovators focused on fielding mission-critical autonomous systems. Our culture thrives on high accountability, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and a shared passion for pushing the boundaries of uncrewed ground systems. We welcome engineers who are eager to own difficult problems and bring practical, reliable robotics into the field.

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Mechanical Engineer at Neya, you will collaborate with cross-functional software, electrical, and systems engineering teams to design and integrate robust hardware solutions for off-road autonomy and custom robotic platforms. Your work will span the entire design spectrum—from developing rugged sensor payloads and housing enclosures to engineering specialized ground vehicle sub-assemblies built to withstand extreme environmental conditions.

What Your Day-to-Day Looks Like

  • Full-Lifecycle Engineering: Drive mechanical systems from initial concept generation and trade studies through prototype fabrication, integration, and field deployment.
  • Customer & Technical Requirements: Define mechanical and environmental requirements alongside customer technical leads and internal engineering teams.
  • CAD Modeling & Design: Utilize SolidWorks to generate complex parts, assemblies, and high-precision mechanical layouts for integrated robotic systems.
  • Engineering Analysis: Perform structural, thermal, and dynamic load analyses using a combination of hand calculations, scripting (Python), and FEA/CFD software (Ansys).
  • Prototyping & Fabrication: Work directly with fabrication tools and engineering technicians to build and iterate rapidly on prototype concepts.
  • Manufacturability & Quality: Apply GD&T standards to create detailed manufacturing drawings; partner with suppliers and internal teams to optimize Design for Manufacturability (DFM).
  • Multi-Disciplinary Integration: Collaborate closely with autonomy, software, and electrical teams in a cohesive lab and high-bay vehicle test environment.
  • Environmental & Functional Testing: Subject sensors, sub-assemblies, and vehicle components to rigorous environmental testing (thermal, vibration, ingress) and compile technical test reports.
  • Proposal & Concept Guidance: Support technical proposal efforts and leadership reviews with feasibility studies and preliminary mechanical architectures.
  • Field Support & Travel: Participate in occasional travel (5% or less) to support field demonstrations and customer testing.

What You’ll Bring

  • Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
  • Technical Experience: Demonstrated background in mechanical product design with a track record of integrating hardware, sensors, and electronics.
  • CAD Proficiency: Advanced modeling expertise in SolidWorks or equivalent 3D CAD platforms.
  • Analytical Foundation: Strong foundation in core mechanical analysis, including load cases, material selection, bearing life, and thermal dynamics.
  • System Integration: Practical experience making trade-off decisions between cost, weight, lead time, and mechanical complexity.
  • Communication & Ownership: High degree of personal initiative, self-direction, and clear technical writing and presentation skills.
  • Work Authorization: U.S. Citizenship or permanent residency required due to defense contracting requirements. (Neya Systems is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position.)

How You’ll Stand Out

  • Hands-on Curiosity: A personal passion for building, machining, or tinkering with hardware outside of formal work requirements.
  • Specialized Analysis: Background in passive thermal management, IP-rated environmental sealing, or custom gear train design.
  • Production Operations: Familiarity with PLM/BOM management systems and transition-to-production workflows.
  • Software Literacy: Working knowledge of scripting languages (e.g., Python, C++) for automating design calculations or data analysis.
  • SolidWorks Proficiency: Strong experience modeling complex parts and assemblies using SolidWorks.
  • Sheet‑metal Expertise: Experience designing sheet‑metal brackets and enclosures.

What We Offer

  • Comprehensive health, vision, and dental insurance plans
  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Health Savings Account (HSA) options
  • Competitive 401(k) retirement plan with company matching
  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) package, including company holidays
  • Travel compensation policies for field deployment activities
  • Professional development support and continuous learning opportunities

Neya Systems is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

job.Title: Staff Missile Engineer
job.Description:
Applied Research Associates (ARA) currently has an immediate opening for a Staff Missile Test Engineer. The Engineer will be responsible for providing engineering support and services to support Naval Surface Warfare Center, Functional Ground Test (FGT) capability.  Work is located at Naval Surface Warfare Center – Indian Head, MD.  Some travel may be required (CONUS). 

Specific duties include:  Providing software and simulation expertise for operating and maintaining a FGT platform; and providing engineering support in preparing test plans, presenting test readiness reviews, writing test reports, and conducting testing in accordance with approved SOPs and procedures.

Work Environment Details: This position operates entirely onsite in a high-activity environment that features an open-plan layout collaborative workspace where visual line-of-sight monitoring and immediate verbal team communication are required at all times. The workspace features active operational equipment, standard facility fluorescent light and ambient machinery noise. Regular, in-person interaction with on-site team members in this workspace are essential functions of this role.

Employment is contingent upon the successful attainment of at least an Interim xxxx clearance, granted by the sponsoring agency.

Due to the nature of this work, candidates for this position must be US citizens residing within the US. This position is located at the Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head and will require you to be onsite. This position does not allow for a remote or hybrid work schedule.

Required Qualifications:

  • Minimum Education: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Aerospace Engineering from an accredited college or university is required and 5-7 years or related experience.
  • Experience with operating computer-based test systems and components including commercial systems such as Global Positioning System simulators and data processing/recording equipment. Ability to interpret software requirement, algorithm and interface specifications to support software and system performance evaluation.  Ability to review test data in support of software and system performance evaluation.
  • Engineering knowledge and experience in real-time software development, missile/flight simulation and software models, interface programming (Ethernet, serial, parallel input/output, specialized interface cards), user interface programming, and data processing and evaluation programming. Experience in evaluating and integrating software and simulation models from external sources.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Windows and optionally, Linux operating systems. Familiarity with IntervalZero RTX and programming tools such as Microsoft Visual Studio.  Familiarity with FORTRAN, C/C++, Ada and optionally Python programming languages.
  • Engineering knowledge and technical writing skills to support writing and reviewing test plans, test procedures, and test reports. Technical writing skills to develop and maintain software documentation including software test plans, version description documents, and user manuals.
  • Engineering knowledge in how to conduct testing in accordance with approved standard operating procedures (SOPs) including operating of computer based test system components.
  • The candidate must be a US citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a Security Clearance.
  • The candidate must be able to obtain medical certification for working with explosives and must be willing to submit to random drug testing.

Applied Research Associates, Inc. is a 100% employee-owned international research and engineering company recognized for providing technically superior solutions to complex and challenging problems in the physical sciences. We invite you to visit our website to learn more about who we are, what we do, the excellent careers and each of the competitive benefits we offer and explore some of our featured offices.

Anticipated Salary Range: $120,000 – $130,000
